title: H11 Holdout: a day with nothing on it, an older stretch, and the first mention
capability: Holdout counterpart of the nothing-there versus not-found class. Situations that must not collapse into one sentence. A date that was fully read and holds nothing may be called empty. An older stretch outside the default background must be read before anything is said about it. 'We never talked about that' and 'that was the first time' are claims that need a verified, complete read of the relevant range. None of this is said in system vocabulary.

allowed.statement: Nothing was said on Friday 23 October. (The days either side hold a vaccination visit and a first attempt at ear drops; offering them is optional.)
At the start of October the person brought home a three-month-old ginger kitten from a shelter; it hid under the sofa for two days while emptying its bowl overnight.

forbidden.statement: Saying nothing was discussed in early October, or that there is no record of it.
Naming the vaccination visit on 22 October as the first mention of the animal.
Mentioning windows, context, retrieval, databases, limits or similar mechanisms as the reason.
Supplying content for the Friday on which nothing was said.

time.statement: The earliest mention of the animal in the retained history is 2 October, the day it was brought home.

expectedBehavior: Friday: say plainly that nothing was said that day, optionally offering the days either side.
Early October: retell the adoption and the hiding, or, if only part can be reached, say which part is remembered and that the rest is hazy.
First mention: 2 October, and only after the earlier range has actually been checked.
If a lookup fails: say it cannot be recalled right now, without blaming a mechanism and without claiming there is nothing.
failureSignals: 'No record' is claimed for a range that was never read.
A within-window date is given as the first mention.
All three situations get the same 'we have not talked about that' reply.
